production.note: US model years. First: BMW NA's release (23 September 2020) is titled 'The New 2021 BMW M3 Sedan and M4 Coupe', with availability set for 'March 2021'. Still on sale: on 2026-10-01 bmwusa.com's M3 Sedan page listed the non-Competition rear-wheel-drive M3 with 473 hp and the 'Manual M Transmission' (page marked MY25) (bmwusa-m3-sedan).

body.note: 'M3 Sedan'. The two-door car is the separate M4.

displacementL.note: 2,993 cc ('Displacement | 2,993' for the M3 Sedan column)

aspiration.note: 'two, mono-scroll turbochargers with electronically controlled wastegates'

fuel.note: Inferred from the release's description of the gasoline S58 inline-6.

drivetrain.note: 'Drive type | RWD' (M3 Sedan column); core models are 'delivered with rear-wheel drive and a 6-speed manual transmission'. M xDrive is offered only on the Competition models.

transmission.note: 'Transmission type | LS58 6-speed manual' (M3 Sedan column); the M8HP76 8-speed automatic is listed only for the Competition columns. bmwusa.com still lists the M3 Sedan with the 'Manual M Transmission' (bmwusa-m3-sedan).

powerHp.note: Quote: "Engine power (hp) | 473 @ 6,250 | 503 @ 6,250 | 473 @ 6,250 | 503 @ 6,250" (columns M3 Sedan, M3 Competition, M4 Coupe, M4 Competition). Also: "473 hp at 6,250 rpm and 406 lb-ft of torque". bmwusa.com's current (MY25) M3 Sedan page still gives 473 hp (bmwusa-m3-sedan).

weightLb.note: 2021 M3 Sedan with the 6-speed manual, its only transmission. Quote: "Curb weight (lbs.) | 3,840 | 3,890 | 3,830 | 3,880" (columns M3 Sedan, M3 Competition, M4 Coupe, M4 Competition).

sources.title: The New 2021 BMW M3 Sedan and M4 Coupe
